items.stem: A playbook task using the shell module reports 'changed' every run even when nothing changed. What is the issue?

options.text: The task is not idempotent and should use a proper module
options.rationale: Correct: shell commands are not idempotent; a dedicated module reports change accurately.

options.text: Ansible always reports changed for every task
options.rationale: Idempotent modules report 'ok' when no change is needed.
A missing inventory would stop execution, not misreport change.
Handlers affect notifications, not change detection on a task.

items.explanation: Correct: shell commands are not idempotent; a dedicated module reports change accurately.

items.stem: Two sources set the same variable. Which generally wins by Ansible precedence?

options.text: An extra-var passed on the command line
options.rationale: Correct: extra-vars have the highest precedence.
Group vars are overridden by higher-precedence sources like extra-vars.
Role defaults are among the lowest precedence.
A comment sets nothing and cannot win.

items.explanation: Correct: extra-vars have the highest precedence.

items.stem: Which TWO practices correctly protect secrets in Ansible? (Select TWO)

options.text: Encrypt sensitive variable files with Ansible Vault
options.rationale: Correct: Vault encrypts secrets at rest in the repository.

options.text: Reference the encrypted file and supply the vault password at run time
options.rationale: Correct: supplying the password at run time decrypts without storing it in plaintext.

options.text: Commit the plaintext password into group_vars
options.rationale: Committing plaintext secrets exposes them in version control.

options.text: Echo the secret in a debug task for every run
options.rationale: Printing secrets leaks them into logs.

items.explanation: Correct: Vault encrypts secrets at rest in the repository. Correct: supplying the password at run time decrypts without storing it in plaintext.
